deliverable: The stance-hold membrane MEASURED: the quasi-static actuator demands at the zero-mapped table poses vs the derived caps. The walk's fall is a torque-budget fact, predicted and confirmed -- and the finding opens the load-provenance question.
method: 11-DOF planar statics per stance node: bodies from the Oku Table-1 segments at the zero-mapped pose; mass matrix + gravity torque from the per-body COM Jacobians; the rolling-law contact planted (welded x,y); the contact reaction solved from the UNACTUATED base rows (the engine's own tau=0 law on base x,y); tau_act = -(G + A^T lambda) per coordinate.

the_deeper_finding: The admitted source data contains its own tension: the GRF closure identity 2*I_stance = BW*T holds at -1.3% (the hindlimbs carry the full weight in the data), yet the measured knee torque peak is 5.31 N.m while the static demand at the SAME table poses is 9+ N.m. Resolution: THE SOURCE WALK IS DYNAMICALLY SUPPORTED -- the inverted-pendulum exchange carries the body through the single-support window; the muscles never hold these poses statically. A static-hold requirement is the WRONG demand model for mid-gait; it IS the right model for the entry instant and any recovery -- and there the caps are 10% short at the entry and 33-60% short through the window.
implications_ranked: 1. THE WALK NEEDS MOMENTUM, NOT BIGGER CAPS: with the source's own dynamics, the caps suffice mid-gait (their sim proved it); the failure is that our entry momentum (KE 3.6 J at the no-skid speed) DISSIPATES before the first full cycle: the measured worst ledger error is 2.99 J (an F-G8 RED in its own right -- the energy accounting itself breaks during the walk, candidate: the poscorr booking under the store-bisection's repeated trial advances). THE NEXT MEMBRANE: close the ledger first (a broken meter cannot tune a walk), then measure the dissipation channels (impact heat, friction, clamp-pin losses) against the injected 3.6 J.

2. CAP PROVENANCE: if a static-recovery capability is wanted (F-G6's push test demands it!), the caps need bipedal-load provenance: the honest rescale is cap_j = 1.25 x peak_j / hindlimb_share with the share derived from the admitted GRF bytes -- but the closure identity says the share is 1.0, so NO rescale is derivable from the admitted data alone; a static-capable walker needs either the quadruped (forelimb load path) or a cap amendment with NEW provenance (named, not derived today).

3. The push-test implication: F-G6's scripted push (0.1 BW) demands capture-or-recover; with statically-infeasible single support, recovery MUST be the capture reflex (kinematic), never torque hold -- consistent with the source architecture.
honest_summary: The stance-hold membrane measured: the caps cannot hold the bipedal walker statically in the single-support window (knee 33-60% over at center), the sim's fall matches joint-for-joint, and the source data proves these poses were never held statically -- the walk is a pendulum. Our pendulum's meter was also broken: the ledger baseline bug (fixed, -0.591 J at tick 0) and a residual 3.5 J leak now characterized to the mechanical terms (bal==stor at every tick) with the work-across-poscorr-jumps as the prime suspect. Next membrane: audit the work integral across positional corrections, then the dissipation channels against the 3.6 J entry KE.

ledger_work_this_wave.prime_suspect: free_step books work as tau*(q_end - q_start) per substep -- including the q jumps made by the positional correction between impacts (the actuator did not cause those displacements): ~tau*delta_q ~ 5e-4 J x ~2500 poscorr events ~ 1.3 J, plus impact-projection impulse interactions; the magnitude is right, the audit is the next membrane's first task
